key_insight: The paper extends the J-integral to 3D quasicontinuum fracture simulations and adds uncertainty quantification so crack-driving force estimates can be validated and trusted in multiscale settings.
engineering_relevance: This gives fracture engineers a practical way to compute energy release rates in atomistic-continuum models, supporting large-scale crack simulations while still resolving tip-scale physics.
method: Implemented the J-integral in QC3D under plane strain using Cauchy-Born-derived stress and strain energy density fields.
Validated results against LEFM and the virtual crack extension method across elastic, nonlinear, and atomically relaxed regimes.
Added a Markov chain Monte Carlo procedure to quantify uncertainty from mesh and integration-domain choices.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with LEFM/VCE in three regimes and close agreement between predicted and Griffith critical energy release rates in a silicon three-point bending simulation.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on mesh quality, integration-domain selection, and plane-strain/Cauchy-Born assumptions, so careful setup is needed for robust results.
paper_title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
